title: Build Specialized Agents on a Stack You Control with NVIDIA NemoClaw | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA NemoClaw is a set of open blueprints that wraps existing agent harnesses (OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, LangChain Deep Agents) with Nemotron models, NeMo optimization tools and the OpenShell policy runtime. The post is product marketing, with the one hard claim being that LangChain's harness tuning brought Nemotron 3 Ultra to near-frontier performance at about 10x lower cost per run.

insights.claim: NemoClaw is not a harness or a runtime but a collection of open blueprints that assembles a tuned harness, Nemotron models, NeMo optimization tools and the OpenShell secure runtime on top of the harness a developer already uses.
insights.speaker: Nicola Sessions
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is positioning itself as the full-stack open agent platform layer, pulling harness users toward Nemotron and NVIDIA runtime software.
insights.quote: NemoClaw is not a competing harness, and it is not a runtime.
insights.locator: Using NemoClaw for full-stack production agents

insights.claim: NemoClaw blueprints currently support three harnesses: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent from Nous Research, and LangChain Deep Agents.
insights.speaker: Nicola Sessions
insights.so_what: These are the harnesses NVIDIA is choosing to partner with; watch which gain enterprise share.

insights.claim: An agent needs four things: a model that reasons, a harness that defines how it operates, tools and skills, and a runtime governing what it can access and do in production.
insights.speaker: Nicola Sessions
insights.so_what: A useful decomposition of the agent stack for mapping vendors and where value accrues.

insights.claim: NVIDIA says a NemoClaw agent can be built without rewriting an existing agent, since a blueprint assembles the surrounding stack around OpenClaw, Hermes Agent or LangChain Deep Agents.
insights.speaker: Nicola Sessions
insights.so_what: Low switching cost lowers the barrier to NVIDIA software attach for existing agent builders.
insights.locator: Using NemoClaw for full-stack production agents

insights.claim: LangChain tuned its Deep Agents harness for Nemotron 3 Ultra by adjusting prompts, tools and middleware without retraining, reaching near-frontier performance at approximately 10x lower cost per run than leading closed models.
insights.speaker: Nicola Sessions
insights.so_what: If it holds, open models with tuned harnesses undercut closed-model per-run cost, a pricing pressure signal for frontier API vendors; it is a vendor-reported claim with no benchmark detail.
insights.quote: brought Nemotron 3 Ultra to near-frontier performance at approximately 10x lower cost per run
insights.locator: Why co-optimizing the model and harness matters

insights.claim: Mismatched model and harness pairs cause agents to ask for context again, stop early or loop without progress, so tuning the harness to a specific model is a source of performance gains.
insights.speaker: Nicola Sessions
insights.so_what: Suggests agent performance gains can come from harness engineering rather than model training, favoring open-model deployers.
insights.locator: Why co-optimizing the model and harness matters

insights.claim: The tuned Nemotron 3 Ultra model profile is available through LangChain on GitHub, so developers get the optimizations without repeating the tuning work.
insights.speaker: Nicola Sessions
insights.so_what: Packaged tuning makes Nemotron more competitive as a default model for Deep Agents users.
insights.locator: Why co-optimizing the model and harness matters

insights.claim: NeMo Relay observes and improves agent execution and exports session trajectories for audit and further optimization, and NeMo tools also provide routing that can improve throughput, cost and reliability.
insights.speaker: Nicola Sessions
insights.so_what: Telemetry and routing are the hooks for a data flywheel that keeps users on NVIDIA's stack.
insights.locator: Example: A memory-driven Chief of Staff

insights.claim: OpenShell is the runtime in every NemoClaw reference, governing agent access to files, networks, credentials and tools, and keeping credentials for managed inference and MCP connections outside the sandbox.
insights.speaker: Nicola Sessions
insights.so_what: Policy enforcement and credential isolation are enterprise gating factors for production agents, and NVIDIA is bundling them.

insights.claim: OpenShell keeps an agent bound by policy even when its memory or retrieved context leads it toward an unintended action.
insights.speaker: Nicola Sessions
insights.so_what: Frames memory and retrieval as an attack and error surface requiring a runtime guard rather than prompt-level safeguards.
insights.quote: keep the agent bound by policy even when its memory or retrieved context leads it toward an unintended action
insights.locator: Example: A memory-driven Chief of Staff

insights.claim: The OpenShell tutorial shows how to create a first policy that prevents data exfiltration to GitHub, with more sophisticated policies in NemoClaw references covering many internal tools, sites and channels.
insights.speaker: Nicola Sessions
insights.so_what: Concrete example of agent egress control as a security product category.

insights.claim: The community NemoClaw repository includes a memory-driven Chief of Staff recipe, built as a Hermes profile, that keeps a persistent human-readable model of people, projects and priorities so context is not rebuilt each task.
insights.speaker: Nicola Sessions
insights.so_what: Persistent memory agents are an emerging reference use case for enterprise assistants.
insights.locator: Example: A memory-driven Chief of Staff

insights.claim: NemoClaw agents can run in the cloud, in data centers, on NVIDIA DGX Spark, and on NVIDIA RTX PCs and workstations.
insights.speaker: Nicola Sessions
insights.so_what: Agent workloads are being used to justify demand for NVIDIA local hardware as well as data center GPUs.
insights.locator: Deploy across cloud, data center, and local systems

insights.claim: NVIDIA expects NemoClaw specialists on open models and owned infrastructure to work alongside frontier agents, with Claude, Codex or Cursor agents delegating domain-specific subtasks to them.
insights.speaker: Nicola Sessions
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is pitching a hybrid architecture where frontier agents orchestrate and cheaper open-model agents execute, relevant to inference demand mix.
insights.locator: Deploy across cloud, data center, and local systems

insights.claim: NVIDIA cites a clinical agent for a hospital and a simulation agent for electronic design automation as examples of different specialized agents running on the same NemoClaw stack.
insights.speaker: Nicola Sessions
insights.so_what: Indicates the vertical targets NVIDIA is marketing agents to: healthcare and EDA.
insights.locator: Deploy across cloud, data center, and local systems
